checks.proof: By Stirling, log n! = n log n - n + O(log n). Hence log(((n!)^{1/(alpha n)})/n) = (1/(alpha n))log n! - log n = (1/alpha - 1)log n - 1/alpha + o(1). If alpha<1, this tends to +infinity, so L(alpha)=infinity. If alpha>1, this tends to -infinity, so L(alpha)=0. If alpha=1, it tends to -1, so L(alpha)=e^{-1}. Therefore L(alpha)=1/e implies alpha=1.

The implication is false. For any alpha>1, the logarithmic expression has coefficient (1/alpha - 1)<0, so it tends to -infinity and L(alpha)=0. For example, alpha=2 gives L(2)=0, while alpha=1 gives L(1)=1/e, not 0.
For alpha=1, log(((n!)^{1/n})/n) = (1/n)log n! - log n = -1 + o(1) by Stirling. Therefore L(1)=e^{-1}=1/e.

The implication is false. From Stirling, L(alpha)=1/e occurs exactly when alpha=1, not alpha=2. Indeed, for alpha=2, log(((n!)^{1/(2n)})/n) = (1/2 - 1)log n - 1/2 + o(1) = -1/2 log n - 1/2 + o(1), which tends to -infinity, so L(2)=0.
